title: Device-targeted feature flags for telemetry ingestion
name: Telemetry flag client

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code loads and evaluates feature flags for devices? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. The fetch is bounded by an AbortController timeout that is always cleared in finally; a failed refresh keeps the last good snapshot instead of clearing it; invalid percentages are skipped rather than poisoning the snapshot; the snapshot is swapped in one assignment so readers never see a half-built map; unknown flags fall back to explicit defaults; bucketing hashes flag key plus device id and uses `< rolloutPercent` over 0-99, so 0% is fully off and 100% fully on; the firmware gate compares numerically, so 1.10 sorts after 1.9.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The flag service is unreachable for ten minutes after the client has started successfully. How does isEnabled behave during that time?
choices: It returns the hard-coded defaults for every flag
It throws until the next successful refresh
It returns false for every flag
It keeps answering from the last successfully fetched snapshot
choiceQuestions.explanation: refresh() only assigns `this.snapshot` after a successful fetch; on error it logs and leaves the old map. Defaults apply only to keys missing from the snapshot, and isEnabled never throws.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A flag has `firmwareMin: "2.10.0"`. A device reports firmware "2.9.4". What does isEnabled return?
choices: false, because 9 < 10 in the second numeric segment
It depends only on the rollout bucket
true, because missing segments default to 0
choiceQuestions.explanation: compareVersions parses segments as integers, so 2 = 2, then 9 - 10 < 0, and the firmware gate returns false before bucketing. A string comparison would wrongly rank 2.9.4 higher; segment padding does not matter here.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does start() call `this.timer.unref()` on the refresh interval?
choices: So the refresh timer alone does not keep the Node.js process alive during shutdown
So refreshes run on a separate thread
So that refresh failures are not logged
To make the interval fire immediately
choiceQuestions.explanation: unref() tells the event loop not to wait on this timer, so the process can exit once other work is done. It does not change threading, logging, or timing of the first tick.
